findings.description: The Knowledge row claims 'pup merge... refreshes the code map in the same transaction,' but `runMergeGate` in `src/core/merge-gate.service.ts` never calls `buildCodeMap` — it only calls `draftDecisionRecord`. `buildCodeMap` (src/core/code-map.service.ts) is invoked only from the `pup map` CLI action and from session-profile compilation, and it's a stateless, live computation with nothing persisted to refresh. Merge does not touch the code map at all.
findings.body:
**Concern:** The "What you get" table states: "Every merge writes a decision record and refreshes the code map in the same transaction." The decision-record half is accurate (`draftDecisionRecord` is called inside `runMergeGate`). The code-map half is not: `buildCodeMap` is called from exactly two places in the whole codebase (`pup map`'s CLI action and session profile compilation) and never from `src/core/merge-gate.service.ts` or anything it calls. It's also a pure, stateless computation each call (live git log + adapter dep graph, nothing cached in the DB), so there is no persisted map for a merge to "refresh" even in principle. This mirrors an already-aspirational line in `docs/04-gates-and-debt.md` ("Knowledge transaction: regenerate code map for touched modules..."), but this PR newly asserts it as present-tense, factual behavior in public-facing marketing copy — a reader has no way to know it doesn't match the shipped implementation.

**Permalink:** https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/e3b256a15094442b6adc2e852edf0dfeeffa8f97/README.md#L44
findings.suggestion: | Knowledge | Every merge writes a decision record. `pup log`, `pup map --open`, `pup report --open` show what exists and why. |

findings.description: Contributing section states 'the pre-commit hook runs the tests' as an unconditional fact, but `scripts/pre-commit` is never wired up automatically: its own header requires `cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit`. There's no `prepare`/`postinstall` script or `.husky/` directory, and the only CI workflow (`claude-code-review.yml`) is an LLM review, not a test runner. AGENTS.md, which this same sentence points readers to, never mentions the hook or its install step either — so a new contributor reading this line has no actual test gate on their commits unless they take an undocumented manual step.
findings.body:
**Concern:** "Work happens on a branch, never on `main`, and the pre-commit hook runs the tests" reads as an active guarantee, but the hook is inert until manually installed: `scripts/pre-commit`'s own header says `Install: cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit`. `package.json` has no `prepare`/`postinstall` script and there's no `.husky/` directory to auto-install it, and `.github/workflows/` has no CI that runs tests on a PR (only the LLM-based `claude-code-review.yml`). `AGENTS.md` — which this same sentence tells contributors to read first — never mentions this hook or its install step; neither does `docs/workflow.md`, which documents the hook's behavior but not how to activate it. A contributor could reasonably believe their commits are already gated by tests and skip running the test suite themselves.

**Permalink:** https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/e3b256a15094442b6adc2e852edf0dfeeffa8f97/README.md#L136
findings.suggestion: Issues and pull requests are welcome. Read [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) first: it is the same brief the project's own sessions get. Work happens on a branch, never on `main`; install the pre-commit hook (`cp scripts/pre-commit .git/hooks/pre-commit && chmod +x .git/hooks/pre-commit`) to run the tests before committing.

findings.description: The design-doc table describes '05 Knowledge layer' as covering 'Code map, decision records, report,' but docs/05-knowledge-layer.md has no section on the `pup report` HTML artifact — that's actually specified in docs/02-cli.md. A reader following the link to learn about `pup report` won't find it there.
